messages:
Sam W.: FYI billing surprised — our Dedicated pool 'pd-nyc-03' shows 1.8k GPU hours debited overnight, dashboard shows ~200 active hours. Invoice lineitem includes reserved_hours: 1600. Anyone seen this? :thinking:

Leila M.: @Sam W. can you paste the pool id and a sample request id? Also which org/account?

Sam W.: org: acme-payments, pool: pd-nyc-03, sample req: req_0a7f2b. Saw spike between 2025-07-02T02:00Z and 2025-07-02T05:30Z. No canary or mass tests scheduled.

Billing Bot: [automated] Invoice 2025-07 for org acme-payments generated. Line item: reserved_gpu_hours: 1600, burst_gpu_hours: 200.

Jordan P.: @Leila M. adding eng-oncall. Could be burst autoscale + delayed metering. Did the pool recently switch to 'best-effort-burst' mode?

Sam W.: Nope, config unchanged. We do have prefix KV cache enabled for streaming; could that keep containers pinned?

Eng Oncall: Hypothesis: long-lived KV caches + pinned worker affinity prevented scale-in; GPU hours were counted while idle but still reserved. Checking autoscaler logs now.

Eng Oncall: Quick check — look at these logs:
```
[autoscaler] 2025-07-02T03:12:14Z scale_down blocked: cache_pinned_workers=4
[worker] 2025-07-02T03:12:14Z pinned_by_request=req_0a7f2b
```

Leila M.: If true, billing should show consumed vs reserved. Can you run this metering query and paste the result?
```
SELECT pool_id, sum(allocated_gpu_seconds) FROM metering.events
WHERE pool_id='pd-nyc-03' AND ts BETWEEN '2025-07-02' AND '2025-07-03'
GROUP BY pool_id;
```

Sam W.: Ran it — returned 6,480,000s (~1800 GPU hours). That matches invoice. But dashboard 'active hours' widget shows 200h. Widget uses 'active_token_processing' not 'allocated_seconds'. Mismatch likely due to allocation metric being charged.

Jordan P.: Ok so root cause: allocation-based billing (includes pinned workers) vs dashboard showing actual token processing. We'll need billing team's help to clarify invoice line items and whether SLA credits apply.

Leila M.: @Billing Bot can you confirm whether reserved_hour debits include pinned idle workers caused by caching? Also request SLA credit if this is a mis-billing.

Billing Bot: [automated] Received support request 98765. Escalating to Billing-Engineering. Estimated response 24-48h. Attaching invoice and meter id.

Sam W.: Thanks. Next steps: eng to add alert for pinned_worker_count and dashboard to surface allocated_gpu_hours. Will follow up with customer-facing note.

Eng Oncall: I'll open ENG-4567 to add metric and short-term fix to allow cache eviction after X minutes of inactivity. /cc @Leila M.

Leila M.: Adding ticket to customer case CS-54211. Marking P2 until clarified. :white_check_mark:
